summary: Jefferson County, FL 100-foot Aermotor tower built 1956; auctioned August 2009 and dismantled September 14-16, 2009; Gum Creek move was only tentative.

facts.status_note: Sold at auction in August 2009 and dismantled in September 2009; sources read do not confirm where the tower stands now

events.note: Land for the tower bought from Otto and Elsa Lorenzen on November 4, 1955
Erected March 1956 by Aermotor of Chicago, 100 feet tall, at a cost of $3,855.29
Article says state lookout positions were closed in 1995 or 1996 and Jefferson County phased out its three towers shortly after
August 2009: sold at auction for $2,102; buyer had 45 days from payment to remove it
Dismantled into sections starting Monday September 14, 2009; by noon September 16 only concrete footers remained
Tentative plan: top 40-foot section with cab to become an observation tower at Gum Creek Hunting Preserve, Madison County; not confirmed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts says only that the tower was dismantled and moved. The 2009 article gives Gum Creek Hunting Preserve as a tentative destination and says the 80-foot tower standing there is the former Ashville tower. No source read confirms the Monticello tower reached Gum Creek.

notes_for_editor: Brief record is correct on height (100 ft = 30.5 m) and design. The article's column text is jumbled; quotes were taken from the cached text. Its paragraph about land bought in 1944 and a tower built in 1945 by International refers to another tower (probably Wacissa), so it was not used. The Forest Lookouts page gives no staffing list. No post-2009 source was found; the site today is unknown. OpenStreetMap node 358719663 still maps a tower point at the location, which does not show that anything stands there.
